svg.title: architect-os: what is ready, and where what comes next will join
svg.desc: The architecture of architect-os in one image, in five parts. Ready marks bricks available on main. Next marks planned work or pending integration beside the brick it will join. 1. The native gateway authenticates each client on loopback and routes its calls to modules and task workers. The gateway starts the data process and the model broker on standard input and output. Only data holds the database URL. Only the model broker holds the API key. A module calls back with its call ID. A worker can reach only the broker and uses a token scoped to its task. 2. Define reads a validated prd-gen handoff over MCP. The admitted planning host can drive a pinned Spec bundle through drafting and independent review and resume from its private journal. Plan accepts the verified Spec proposal or a draft from Claude Code, Codex or Antigravity. It can also import a completed Antigravity exchange. Plan previews one Step. A plain proposal can be materialized with local approval. The independently reviewed Spec projection stops at preview. Step verifies a separate host receipt for its inputs, target tree, launcher, independent reviews and prompt specimens. The host verifies scout citations against repository lines before including them in the Builder brief. The orchestration loop takes a brief, those verified facts, a build session, checks without a model, the replay of the host, reviews that cannot write the worktree, the gate, and the delivery of the same commit to the branch and then to main; after a refusal, the orchestrator writes a new brief; the host writes steps/<name>/ into the worktree. The production Step runs Claude Code under SRT. In a separate Docker SBX Linux VM, the offline bench verifies both a Codex file write and a read-only fixture turn. The Gemini client (Antigravity) exits 1 at offline session creation. In trial 9, the account owner authorized the host once. The host renewed the account-bound grant once and checked the account catalog twice. The pinned Codex client calculated a different checksum in each of two fresh VMs. Both commands exited 0 and the host verified both results. For a third VM, the host sent one Astra subscription request. The provider completed the response and reported 39 input and 31 output tokens. The host withheld the text because it could not interpret the moderation report. Codex exited 1. The host found all three workspaces empty after shutdown. Six of the nine single-request trials yielded a provider completion with measured token usage. Monetary cost is unknown. A subscription turn that delivers text and a production Builder in SBX remain pending. 3. The isolation diagram places the host beside two separate runtimes. SRT isolates production Step sessions and the gateway’s modules and workers in OS processes under five profiles. Docker SBX creates a Linux VM for the qualification bench. Its unprivileged native client exchanges requests and responses with the host over standard input and output. The host holds the account-bound grant in memory and verifies the account on renewal. Only the host checks provider controls and verifies the native receipt and VM removal. The Builder writes the worktree while the host controls Git metadata. Host Git sources attributes from the empty tree. The fingerprint, Gate and Deliver check for visible nested Git markers before untracked discovery. The Gate lease and Deliver also compare checkout bytes with the commit. The authentication proxy on the host gives the Claude session a scoped token so the credential stays on the host throughout the session. The required ./aos entry checks the marked runtime root and the available space on the root and home filesystems before npm, then records admission in the new run directory. Repository automation uses this entry. All five profiles use private session directories. The host retains Step results and journals under the root and writes raw streams to the run temporary directory. Gate locks each physical checkout, writes to its run reports directory, and retains the checked Linux receipt for Deliver. A canary under the same profile must fail before each command. What each profile opens is the generated image isolation-profiles.svg, held equal to the five profile files by the gate. 4. Five checks before the gate, then the host gate and npm run deliver. In CI, Linux splits the full scenario suite into two shards and checks mutants in sixteen lanes with independent replay. macOS runs the sandbox scenarios. 5. The evidence desk verifies each DOI at doi.org and matches normalized passages in the supplied full text; the watch of Anthropic compares the public sources the platform relies on with a committed register.

SRT · production Step and gateway processes
The host proxy revokes the random session token when the session ends.
The Builder writes its worktree. Reviewer and scout sessions are read-only.
Checks run commands under the checker profile.
Five profiles · builder, reviewer, checker, module and worker
Each profile has private session folders and the same denied read paths.
Its file defines writes, network destinations and credentials. The gateway
starts one process per module and a fresh worker for each task run.
Before each command, the same profile must deny a sibling secret and
an unlisted loopback port. A failed canary stops the command. The suite
tests eight attacks per profile and three Builder writes to steps/.

Codex reaches the host over stdin/stdout. Network egress is blocked.
